questions.question:
In namespace `rbac-test`:

1. Create a Role named `pod-manager` that allows `get`, `list`, `watch`, `create` and `delete` on `pods` (and nothing else).
2. Bind this Role to user `alice` with a RoleBinding named `pod-manager-binding`.
3. Verify with `kubectl auth can-i ... --as=alice`: alice must be able to manage pods inside `rbac-test` only - she must NOT be able to read secrets anywhere, nor touch pods in other namespaces.

verification.description: Role pod-manager grants exactly get,list,watch,create,delete on pods
RoleBinding pod-manager-binding binds Role pod-manager to user alice
can-i as alice: manage pods in rbac-test only - secrets and other namespaces denied

questions.question:
In namespace `sa-token`:

1. Create a ServiceAccount named `app-sa`.
2. Create a Pod named `sa-pod` (image `nginx:1.27`) that runs under this ServiceAccount.
3. The pod must be Running, and the ServiceAccount token must be mounted at the standard path `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/` - verify the mounted token really belongs to `app-sa`.

verification.description: ServiceAccount app-sa exists and pod sa-pod uses it (serviceAccountName)
Pod sa-pod is Running with image nginx:1.27
Service account token is mounted in the pod and its subject is app-sa

questions.question:
A Kustomize base lives at `/tmp/exam/kustomize/base` on `ckad9999` - it defines a Deployment and a Service and sets the target namespace.

1. Apply the KUSTOMIZATION (not the raw YAML files) so that ALL resources it defines are created in namespace `kustomize-demo`.
2. The Deployment must end up with 2 replicas of `nginx:1.27`, and the Service must select the Deployment's pods on port 80.
3. No copies of these resources may be left in the `default` namespace.

verification.description: Deployment webapp and Service webapp exist in kustomize-demo, nothing stray in default
Deployment webapp has 2 replicas of nginx:1.27
Service webapp selects the Deployment pods and exposes port 80

questions.question:
In namespace `init-shared` create a Pod named `init-pod`:

1. An **init container** named `init-container` (image `busybox:1.36`) running `sh -c 'echo "Init complete" > /shared/init.txt'`, writing into an emptyDir volume named `shared-vol` mounted at `/shared`.
2. A main container named `main-container` (image `nginx:1.27`) that mounts the SAME volume `shared-vol` at `/usr/share/data`.
3. The init container must finish (exit 0) before the main container starts, and `/usr/share/data/init.txt` inside the running pod must contain `Init complete`.

verification.description: Init container init-container (busybox:1.36) runs the echo command as defined
emptyDir shared-vol mounted at /shared by init and /usr/share/data by main container
Init container completed, pod Running, and /usr/share/data/init.txt says 'Init complete'

questions.question:
In namespace `env-demo`:

1. Create a ConfigMap named `app-config` with keys `APP_ENV=production` and `LOG_LEVEL=info`.
2. Create a Secret named `db-secret` with key `DB_PASSWORD=supersecret`.
3. Create a Pod named `config-pod` (image `nginx:1.27`, container named `config-pod`) that exposes BOTH in the main container's environment: all keys of `app-config` via `envFrom`, and `DB_PASSWORD` via a single `env` entry sourced from the Secret.
4. The pod must be Running with all three values visible in its environment.

verification.description: ConfigMap app-config has APP_ENV=production and LOG_LEVEL=info
Secret db-secret has DB_PASSWORD=supersecret
Pod config-pod uses envFrom for app-config and env/secretKeyRef for DB_PASSWORD
Pod Running and APP_ENV, LOG_LEVEL, DB_PASSWORD visible in the container env

questions.question:
In namespace `dynamic-storage`:

1. Create a PersistentVolumeClaim named `dynamic-pvc` requesting `1Gi` with `ReadWriteOnce` that uses the cluster's **default StorageClass** (find it with `kubectl get storageclass` - the one marked `(default)`).
2. Create a Pod named `storage-pod` (image `nginx:1.27`) mounting the claim at `/data`.
3. The claim must end up `Bound` to a dynamically provisioned volume, and the pod must be Running with the volume mounted at `/data`.

verification.description: PVC dynamic-pvc: 1Gi ReadWriteOnce on the cluster's default StorageClass
PVC Bound to a dynamically provisioned volume from that StorageClass
Pod storage-pod Running with dynamic-pvc mounted at /data

questions.question:
In namespace `secure` create a NetworkPolicy named `deny-all` that blocks ALL traffic to and from every pod in the namespace:

1. It must select ALL pods (`podSelector: {}`).
2. It must cover BOTH directions - Ingress and Egress.
3. It must define no allow rules at all: with this policy in place nothing in `secure` can receive or initiate traffic.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy deny-all exists in secure with podSelector {} (all pods)
policyTypes includes both Ingress and Egress
No ingress and no egress allow rules are defined

questions.question:
Pod `bad-image` in namespace `image-pull` never starts: it was created with a wrong image reference and is stuck failing to pull it.

1. The intended image is `nginx:1.27` - fix the pod so it pulls and runs.
2. Keep the pod named `bad-image` in namespace `image-pull`; it must end up Running and Ready.

verification.description: Pod bad-image now uses image nginx:1.27
Pod bad-image is Running and Ready
Pod still has a single container named bad-image

questions.question:
Pod `pending-pod` in namespace `pending-lab` has been stuck `Pending` since it was created.

1. Diagnose it: its `nodeSelector` requires the label `workload=batch`, and no node carries that label yet.
2. The ops team wants this pod to run on node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` - make it schedulable there by labelling the node.
3. Do NOT delete, recreate or edit the pod - its identity must not change. Fix it at the node.

verification.description: Node k3d-cluster-agent-1 carries the label workload=batch
Pod pending-pod is Running on k3d-cluster-agent-1
Pod identity preserved (same UID as recorded at setup - pod was not recreated)

questions.question:
Pod `multi-app` in namespace `logs` has two containers: `app` (which produces numbered log lines) and `sidecar` (which emits unrelated noise).

1. Save the **last 100 lines** of the `app` container's logs - only that container's logs - to `/tmp/exam/outputs/multi-app-logs.txt` on `ckad9999` (create the directory if needed).
2. The file must contain exactly those 100 lines in order, and nothing from the sidecar container.

verification.description: File exists with exactly 100 lines
Content is app-line-51 through app-line-150 in order (the last 100 lines)
File contains no sidecar container output
